newsitem.title: ITALY: No alternatives to Serbia election results-Gonzalez.
newsitem.headline: No alternatives to Serbia election results-Gonzalez.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, who led an international mission to Belgrade, said on Tuesday the Serbian must fully reinstate opposition election victories it annulled.
Gonzalez told a meeting of the International Socialist movement in Rome he had received Serbian Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic a week ago and had been invited to return to Belgrade.

The former Spanish leader headed a mission of the Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) which confirmed opposition local election victories in 14 towns and demanded the authorities recognise them.

"I said I would only go if I were invited by the international community to apply the conclusions of (my) report and I rejected alternative formulas...I don't think there are alternative formulas," Gonzalez told the meeting.

President Slobodan Milosevic's decision to annul the victory of the Zajedno (Together) coalition in local polls in Belgrade and 13 other cities on November 17, citing "irregularities", has sparked nine weeks of street protests and international condemnation.
Milosevic invited the OSCE to send a mission to Belgrade but has yet to implement the findings of Gonzalez's mission.

Vesna Pesic, one of Zajedno's co-leaders, told Reuters at the Rome meeting of international leftist parties and groups that negotiations with Milosevic could only begin once the election results had been reinstated.
"It (the situation) is completely stuck now," she said. "We cannot negotiate about the elections because it is not a negotiable thing," she said.
"We certainly will be keeping the pressure up from this side all the time," she added.

Serbian courts dealt Zajedno a double blow on Monday by suspending a ruling declaring that Milosevic's Socialists had lost municipal elections in Belgrade and handing them victory in another disputed town.
